content.text: The text surveys major Civil War campaigns: Chickamauga and Chattanooga, where Thomas held the “Rock” and Grant defeated Bragg; Grant and Lee’s Wilderness, Spotsylvania, Cold Harbor, and Petersburg campaigns; Sherman’s advance from Chattanooga to Atlanta, his March to the Sea, and campaign through the Carolinas; Sheridan’s Shenandoah victories; and the final collapse of the Confederacy. It recounts decisive battles, immense casualties, logistical innovation, devastation, and leadership by Thomas, Grant, Lee, Sherman, Sheridan, and others. Lee evacuated Richmond and Petersburg, retreated through Virginia, and surrendered to Grant at Appomattox on April 9, 1865. The text also includes dramatic scenes from a Belgian play about flooding dams to resist invading German forces, followed by a railroad-accident discussion emphasizing telegraphic safety, signaling failures, and collisions.
